x_pinakes.title: Pinakes capability manifest — the canonical resolver/producer on the Koine capability bus
x_pinakes.description: The KCB (`koine/specs/capability-bus.md` §2) manifest Pinakes publishes as the authority provider named in that spec's §6 per-project mapping. It is a SURFACE WRAPPER, not an implementation: every capability below points at code that is already built and merged (the Wikidata OpenRefine reconciler `engine/src/pinakes_engine/schema/reconcile.py`, the csid resolver `services/api/src/pinakes/search/graph_resolver.py`, the graph query layer `services/api/src/pinakes/engine/`, and the canonical-TSV / entity-grounding exporters under `scripts/`). Nothing here re-implements a reconciler. The manifest exists so a consumer can DISCOVER those surfaces through the bus; because §3 is route-by-lookup rather than proxy, a consumer that cannot reach the orchestrator-hosted registry can read this document from Pinakes directly (`/.well-known/kcb-manifest.json`) and invoke the same endpoints — Pinakes never depends on the registry to serve its capabilities. The same rule governs the `finetune` capability added in 0.3.0: it points at the already-built trainer, which since 0.3.1 lives in the private `lugh` repo (`lugh:pinakes-train-slm` — one console script carrying both admission and training, extracted from this repo's `ml/` workspace). lugh stays the sole trainer; the app-side surface advertises and describes it, and since the cutover no longer dispatches to it (see the `finetune` capability's first surface). This entry is TRANSITIONAL: it is retired once lugh publishes its own manifest as `lugh:agent:finetune`, and until then Pinakes keeps advertising so the fabric is never left with no finetune provider.
x_pinakes.endpointNote: Pinakes fronts the KCB §6 capabilities as MCP tools at `endpoints.mcp` (`/mcp`, official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`) and as A2A skills on the agent-card at `endpoints.a2a` (`/.well-known/agent-card.json`, official `@a2a-js/sdk`) in addition to plain HTTP (`endpoints.http`); the agent-card also carries this whole manifest as a `https://koine.dev/kcb/manifest/0.3` AgentCard extension (KCB §2). The per-capability `x_surfaces` are the already-built routes the MCP tools, the A2A skills, and the HTTP base all front; they are the direct-invocation path the §3 registry hands out addresses for.
x_pinakes.egressNote: The dialect every knowledge port below emits, and the per-record-class exportable/local-only assignment behind it, are NOT decided here: `x_pinakes.egressPolicy` points at Pinakes's own egress policy (KGP §7.1/§7.2, koine ADR-0007 facet 3), which is the single in-repo source of truth for both. `assertValidCapabilityManifest` reads the dialect out of that document and rejects any port that disagrees, and `assertFinetuneCapability` reads the `finetune` capability's advertised egress from its `slm-training-corpora` record class — so this manifest can never carry a second, divergent copy of the policy. The participant declaration `contracts/participant.json` names the same file for the same reason.
x_pinakes.authNote: `auth.grants_required` fixes the KCB §5 grant SHAPE only. Grant issuance and spend ceilings live in the orchestrator's workforce governance; Pinakes's own HTTP surfaces keep enforcing their existing `services/api/src/pinakes/contributions/auth.py` policy until a grant issuer exists.
x_pinakes.specializationNote: KFT (`koine/specs/fine-tuning.md`) is deliberately MULTI-PROVIDER (§9, FT-K): agora hosts the *general* trainer, Pinakes runs its own NARROW, specialized `finetune` provider over the lugh QLoRA pipeline (the private `lugh` repo, formerly this repo's `ml/` workspace). The `x_specialization` block on that capability is what lets the §3 registry tell the two apart and route an SLM rule-authoring / neurosymbolic job here rather than to the general trainer. Pinakes's SLM corpora are `synthetic`/`proprietary`/`personal` tier, so the provider resolves LOCAL-ONLY under the §4.2 egress gate and refuses any cross-boundary `compute.class` — the complement to agora's cloud-capable leg, not a competitor to it.
x_pinakes.signingNote: KCB §5 says manifests SHOULD be signed. The served/published manifest is signed over a canonical serialization (`signature` excluded) by `services/api/src/pinakes/kcb/signing.py` (Ed25519) when `PINAKES_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` is configured, populating `signing.key_id` + a detached `signature`; with no key it degrades to `signing.key_id: null` (unsigned) — the authored document below stays unsigned and is the pre-signing source. `signing.alg` is fixed to `ed25519` and shares the shape KGP `manifest.signing` uses.

produces.description: The canonical node/edge TSV bundle — typed Neo4j-import headers from `contracts/canonical-schema.json`, csid-keyed, with the four provenance columns on every row. Grounding-only: reference data a consumer grounds against, never runtime logic.

The entity-grounding pack (csid, entity type, aliases, reconciliation, provenance, licence classes) in the KGP `koine/specs/grounding-pack.md` §2 envelope: content-addressed `pack_id`, `worlds`/`kind`/`basis`/`dialect`, `exact_match` anchor assertions carrying §3 claim ids, and a §7.1 `license_policy` manifest. Contract: `docs/grounding-pack.md`.

Canonical real-world entity references (csids). KINP §6 names Pinakes the single canonical authority for real-world entities, so this port is the one every other project's `same_as` anchors point at. The list is total over `contracts/canonical-schema.json` nodeTypes and is drift-checked by `assertValidCapabilityManifest`.

consumes.description: Grounding-only knowledge from peer producers (media-analysis extraction deltas, Insimul world facts downshifted for export). Arrives through the contribution review queue, never as a live write — KCB §5 merge-review linkage.
Entity references to resolve or reconcile, in any canonical type.

capabilities.name: resolve
capabilities.description: Resolve a Pinakes entity reference (canonical node type + local `pinakes_id`, or a name) to its canonical `cs:<type>:<local>` csid — the KINP entity CURIE per `docs/canonical-schema.md` §3.1. Exact alias hits resolve at confidence 1.0; a tie between distinct csids returns no match rather than guessing.

x_surfaces.description: Entity ref → csid, with the resolution method and confidence.
Permanent entity id → canonical descriptor + canonical URL.

capabilities.name: reconcile
capabilities.description: Reconcile a name-anchored row against Wikidata through the OpenRefine-style reconciliation API and, on a confident match, stamp the QID and re-mint the csid as QID-anchored — which is what collapses two sources onto one identity. KINP §6.1 makes Wikidata the primary real-world anchor; this is the resolver authority behind it.

x_surfaces.description: Runs the Wikidata acquisition + reconciliation pipeline for one domain; every matched/ambiguous/none decision is recorded in the row's provenance and lands in the contribution review queue.
The reconcilable domains + their Wikidata classes (the input vocabulary for the POST above).

capabilities.name: query
capabilities.description: Query the canonical graph corpus — Datalog over the constrained-Horn projection, Cypher over Neo4j, lexical search, and GraphRAG neighborhood retrieval. Answers are grounding-only: facts about consensus reality, not evaluable runtime logic.

x_surfaces.description: Read-only Cypher against the Neo4j projection.
Lexical search over the graph corpus.

capabilities.name: finetune
capabilities.description: Fine-tune a small language model on Pinakes's neurosymbolic training corpora — the SPECIALIZED, local-only leg of the KFT multi-provider program (`koine/specs/fine-tuning.md` §9, FT-K; agora hosts the general trainer). Admits `text-generation` × {sft, lora, qlora} over the knowledge plane and nothing else, and refuses at admission (KFT §3.1, FT-F) anything outside that. Because the SLM corpora are `synthetic`/`proprietary`/`personal` tier, every run resolves LOCAL-ONLY under the §4.2 egress gate and a cross-boundary `compute.class` is refused with a report before any compute. On completion the tuned model is minted as a KINP `model` entity and its adapter / merged / GGUF artifacts as KMI weight assets (§5.1/§5.3), all inheriting the run's egress + union license (§5.4).

inputs.description: The KINP `model` entity to tune (KFT §5.1). Resolved to its Hub coordinate through the entity's external anchor in lugh's `configs/kft-base-models.json` — a bare `hf:model:…` coordinate string is refused, never resolved (FT-G).

KGP pack ids for the rule-SFT / lore-QA training records (KFT §4.1 — references, never inlined payloads). The dataset header's trust tier and license drive the §4.2 egress gate and the §4.3 union license.

outputs.description: The minted KINP `model` entity for the tuned model — `based_on`/`derived_from` the base, anchored on the run's PROV activity + seed + config_hash (KFT §5.2, FT-C).

The adapter / merged-fp16 weights and the Q4_K_M GGUF export as KMI assets, with the §5.3 export-matrix lineage (`media:derived_from` / `media:variant_of`). Content-addressed; an artifact this run did not produce is reported as pending, never minted as a placeholder.

x_specialization.description: The FT-K tiebreak signal. A job carrying an SLM rule-authoring / neurosymbolic specialization (or naming Pinakes explicitly) routes here; a generic `text-generation` job with no specialization signal belongs to agora's general trainer. `egress: local-only` is a refusal posture, not a preference — Pinakes owns no cloud placement.

x_surfaces.description: MCP tools `finetune` / `finetune_subscribe` — ADVERTISED AND DESCRIBED HERE, DISPATCHED BY THE SURFACE BELOW. The wrapper that shelled out to `uv run --project $LUGH_ROOT pinakes-train-slm --kft-job <manifest>` and parsed its `kft-telemetry.jsonl` / `kft-run.json` was `server/services/finetune-provider.ts`, and it retired with the Express backend (tasks/chief/80-cutover.json US-2): this service reaches every backend by import and spawns no child process, so an invoke here degrades with a message naming lugh's console script. The advertisement stays because a describe surface that dropped it would tell a router Pinakes is not a finetune provider at all — and the entry is transitional regardless, retiring when lugh publishes its own KCB manifest.

The `pinakes-train-slm --kft-job` console script the wrapper dispatches to — the sole trainer, in the private `lugh` repo (resolved from `LUGH_ROOT`), NOT a path in this repo. Exit 0 = ran, exit 2 = refused at admission with a machine-readable report on stdout.
The same capability as an A2A skill on the agent-card, mirroring this entry's description + specialization tags.
